parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of gender expression or same-sex conduct; comprehensive anti-discrimination law (2010, expanded 2020) and a gender-identity hate-crime amendment (2013) are in force, with documented but slow remedies (one ruling in favour, a reprimand issued). No universal-exposure measure is documented: no facility/birth-sex rule, no police targeting of trans visitors, no border document friction. Against that: constitutional SOGI protections removed in 2016, complaints machinery slow and distrusted, and documented societal hostility (majorities opposing public LGBT expression; dated 2010-2016 polls plus a 2022 figure). The ten logged trans bias cases lack a background rate, so magnitude is unestablished; political rhetoric is hostility but not organised targeting. Document/gender-marker handling is an open question, not an exposure. The balance is functioning-but-uneven protection with real social disapproval: reduced-risk, but mid-band.
